**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Subject: Religious Studies (code 0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Paper 2: The Old Testament/Jewish Bible and World Faiths. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Sections of the paper: 1.0 The Old Testament/Jewish Bible, Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David (questions 1 to 6); Section 5.3 Islam (questions 7 to 12); Section 5.5 African Traditional Beliefs and Practices (questions 13 to 18).

questions.enonce_markdown: Analyse Moses' reluctance to return to Egypt and how Yahweh convinced him. (25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** At the burning bush (Exodus 3 and 4) God commissioned Moses, then a shepherd in Midian, to bring Israel out of Egypt. Moses made several objections. The passage shows both his human weakness and God's patience in answering each one.

**1. Reasons for Moses' reluctance.**
- *Sense of unworthiness:* "Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh?" (Exodus 3). He had been raised in Pharaoh's house but was now a fugitive, and he had killed an Egyptian (Exodus 2).
- *Fear of the people's doubt:* he had no proof of authority. "They will not believe me." The Hebrews had earlier rejected his interference (Exodus 2).
- *Not knowing God's name:* he asked what to say if the Israelites asked who sent him.
- *Poor speaking ability:* "I am slow of speech and slow of tongue" (Exodus 4).
- *Open refusal:* "Please send someone else". God's anger was kindled at this point.
- *Fear for his life:* the Pharaoh who sought to kill him had died, but Egypt was still a dangerous place.

**2. How Yahweh answered him.**
- *Promise of presence:* "I will be with you", with the sign that Israel would worship God on that mountain.
- *Revelation of the divine name:* "I AM WHO I AM" and the name Yahweh, God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, linking the call to the covenant with the patriarchs.
- *Signs:* the rod turned into a serpent, the hand made leprous and healed, and water becoming blood, to show Moses' authority to Israel.
- *Answer to the speech problem:* "Who gave man his mouth?" God promised to be with Moses' mouth and appointed his brother Aaron as spokesman.
- *Reassurance:* the men who wanted to kill him were dead (Exodus 4).
- *Warning and command:* God showed anger at the final excuse, but still did not drop him.

**3. Assessment.** The narrative displays a pattern common to calls of prophets: reluctance, divine reassurance, then obedience. Moses finally accepted, took his wife and sons and set out for Egypt. His humility prepared him to lead, since he knew the work depended on God.

**Conclusion.** Moses' reluctance came from humility, fear and self-doubt, but God met every objection with promises, signs and a helper, making Moses a willing instrument of the Exodus.
